title: Define contractual (hard enforced) autoscaling bounds vs platform recommended ranges (soft) + Console messaging
creator: Benji Okafor
description:
Decision ticket to remove ambiguity across product/eng/design/sales about what is *hard enforced* vs *advisory* for Dedicated autoscaling.

Why this matters
- Enterprise Dedicated deals (Northstar Fintech / Polaris / Lumen) are explicitly asking for *contractual* spend ceilings + baseline capacity guarantees. We need crisp semantics we can put in docs, Console copy, and (when needed) contract language.
- The platform also wants to offer an opinionated “recommended range” to prevent common misconfigs (min too low causing cold-start queueing; max too high causing spend surprises) without blocking power users.

Scope
- Define which settings are *hard enforced* (autoscaler clamps) vs *soft recommended* (warnings + guidance).
- Define how Console should communicate “platform recommended range” relative to enforced bounds.
- Define API behavior at validation time vs runtime (including shortage/min-unmet edge case).

Non-goals
- Negotiating contract language or approvals flow (Sales/CS owned).
- Defining the exact algorithm for recommendations (tracked separately in autoscaler/signal work).

Decision
1) Hard enforced bounds (customer-configured)
- Fields: min_replicas, max_replicas (or equivalent GPU quota abstraction if/when added).
- Semantics: Always enforced by autoscaler via clamping.
  - desired_raw = output of autoscaler signal arbitration (reactive + predictive)
  - desired_bounded = clamp(desired_raw, min_replicas, max_replicas)
  - autoscaler must never provision > max_replicas.
  - autoscaler must never intentionally scale below min_replicas.
- Precedence: Customer-enforced bounds take precedence over platform defaults, predictive suggestions, and operator/automation recommendations.
- Validation (control plane):
  - Reject update if min_replicas > max_replicas.
  - Reject update if either < 0.
  - If max_replicas == 0, reject for Dedicated (no scale-to-zero); exceptions require internal override only (separate ticket).
- Runtime exception handling:
  - If underlying regional capacity shortage prevents meeting min_replicas, system must:
    - continue retry with backoff
    - surface explicit “min bound unmet” degraded state (for Console + alerts)
    - emit metrics/audit reason so customer + oncall can distinguish “policy issue” vs “infra shortage”.

2) Platform recommended range (soft, advisory)
- Definition: A computed range (recommended_min, recommended_max) shown to the user to guide configuration.
- Not enforced: Recommendations do not clamp the autoscaler and do not block saving (except when violating invariants like min>max).
- When out of recommended range:
  - If enforced min < recommended_min: show warning: likely queueing/latency risk during ramps; suggestion to raise min.
  - If enforced max > recommended_max: show warning: likely spend risk; suggestion to lower max.
  - If enforced max < recommended_min: show strong warning: configuration likely cannot meet typical ramp; suggest either raising max or disabling stricter SLO commitments.
- Source-of-truth: Recommendations are read-only outputs from platform; they are not part of the contractual policy object.
- Updates: Recommendations may change as traffic patterns change; Console must show “last computed” timestamp and a short rationale line.

3) Console / UI communication (what we will implement)
- The policy form inputs are labeled as “Enforced bounds”.
  - “Minimum replicas (enforced)” input
  - “Maximum replicas (enforced)” input
  - Tooltip copy explicitly states: “These bounds are hard limits. The autoscaler will not scale below/above these values.”
- The “platform recommended range” is shown as:
  - Inline helper text under the inputs (e.g., “Recommended: 4–16 replicas”) plus a “Why?” popover.
  - Visual banding in the capacity chart (if present): shaded recommended zone, with the current enforced min/max overlaid.
  - Warning states when enforced values fall outside recommended range (no save-block).
- Copy requirements:
  - Avoid “guarantee” language for recommendations.
  - Recommendations should say “Based on recent traffic + model profile; may change” (and include the timestamp).

4) API / contract surfaces
- Control plane ScalingPolicy object contains only enforced configuration (min/max/cooldowns/predictive toggle), with deterministic evaluation + audit.
- Recommendations are delivered via a separate read-only endpoint or embedded read-only fields with explicit naming (e.g., recommended_min_replicas, recommended_max_replicas, recommended_reason, recommended_as_of).
  - Must be clear these are non-contractual and can change.
- Audit logs must record:
  - who/when updated enforced bounds
  - before/after values
  - autoscaler decisions must record desired_raw, desired_bounded, and “bounded_by=min|max|none” as part of the decision reasoning.

Open questions (resolved here)
- Q: Can the platform ever override customer max in emergencies?
  - A: No. Max is a hard ceiling. If customer is saturating at max, we surface it (alerts + Console) and recommend raising max / adding capacity.
- Q: Can we block saving if user is far outside recommended range?
  - A: No (initially). We warn. We only block for invariants (min>max, negative, scale-to-zero).
- Q: Are recommendations “defaults” for customers that don’t set bounds?
  - A: Defaults are platform-driven behavior (back-compat). Recommendations are guidance; when bounds are unset, the autoscaler continues current behavior until customer opts in.

Acceptance criteria
- ADR updated to clearly separate enforced bounds vs recommendations and capture wording constraints.
- Console copy and UX states agreed with Design (DES-981) and Product (Lauren).
- Control plane API plan: recommendations are read-only and explicitly marked non-contractual.
- Sales/CS enablement note: how to explain “hard” vs “recommended” to customers (linked to CS playbook ticket).

Implementation follow-ups (tracked elsewhere)
- ENG-22144: Console UI for scaling policy config (add “enforced” labeling + warnings + recommended display)
- ENG-22141: Control plane API/schema (ensure recommendations are read-only, enforce invariant validation)
- ENG-22146: Audit events (include bounded_by and desired_raw vs desired_bounded)
- ENG-22151: Region shortage behavior when min bound cannot be met (degraded state + alerting)
comments: 2025-06-26 (Lauren Bishop): Please make sure this aligns with enterprise messaging: customers will interpret “recommended” as a promise unless we’re explicit. Also need a clear statement: max will never be exceeded, even during incidents.

2025-06-28 (Tessa Morgan): UX proposal: label inputs “Enforced bounds” and show recommended as helper text + shaded region on chart. Warnings only, do not block save. Add a “Why this is recommended” popover with (traffic window, model, region).

2025-07-01 (Rafael Mendes): From SRE perspective: hard max is critical. If customer saturates at max we need alerting that doesn’t page-loop—recommend: page only when queue depth sustained AND bound-hit sustained. Also must distinguish min-unmet due to capacity shortage vs policy validation errors.

2025-07-03 (Jordan Lee): Drafted decision language for ADR: ‘recommended range is advisory and may change; enforced bounds are the only contractual inputs.’ Will add requirement that recommendations must be served with timestamp + reason string.

2025-07-08 (Vanessa Ortiz): +1 to no platform override of max. If we ever need an emergency override, it should be an explicit customer-approved action, not silent. For now we’ll treat “max” as invariant in autoscaler clamp.

2025-07-15 (Naomi Feldman): Compliance note: keep “recommended” out of audit trails that might be interpreted as policy. Audit should record only enforced config changes + autoscaler decisions and bounded reasons.

2025-08-15 (Jordan Lee): Marking done. Decision incorporated into ADR text and shared with Console team. Next actions are in ENG-22144 (UI copy + warning states) and ENG-22141 (read-only recommendation fields/endpoint).
